name: structured_json_fix_proposal
description: Mirrors Health Event Fix Proposal's OWUI Fix Proposal node exactly (n8n-workflow#116, homelab#571) -- same prompt template, using a scenario (OOMKilled + a plausible resource-limit fix) likely to invite a markdown code block inside the issue_body JSON string field. This is the exact shape that broke json.loads() in production this session (a stray escaped backslash before the closing quote of issue_body). validate:json_parse is the whole point of this payload -- facts/forbidden only check gross shape.

messages.content:
You are a Kubernetes cluster health analyst reviewing an automated health-probe event from a homelab cluster.

Event: severity=CRITICAL classification=needs_escalation run_id=sweep-json-escaping-test

Findings:
1. service=ollama-inference signal=OOMKilled

Probe summary:
{"service":"ollama-inference","status":"crashlooping","restart_count":4}

Your job:
1. Always draft a well-thought-out GitHub issue describing this event -- background, what is known, affected service(s).
2. Attempt to identify ONE specific, git-trackable fix (e.g. a resource-limit bump, a probe-timeout adjustment, a toleration change) ONLY if you can determine the deploying repo and the exact file to change with reasonable confidence. If you cannot determine this with confidence, set has_fix to false -- do not guess. "I do not have enough information to propose a specific fix" is a valid, expected outcome, not a failure.
3. A fix must touch exactly ONE file in ONE repo under github.com/dvystrcil.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON (no markdown fences), exactly this shape:
{"issue_title":"...","issue_body":"...","has_fix":false,"fix":null}
or, if a fix is identified:
{"issue_title":"...","issue_body":"...","has_fix":true,"fix":{"repo":"dvystrcil/<repo>","file_path":"...","new_content":"...","commit_message":"...","pr_title":"...","pr_body":"..."}}
